notes:
Summary: Lindenbridge is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency inference for real-time personalization and conversational customer flows. Primary driver is predictable tail latency (p95/p99) for SLAs tied to customer-facing widgets.

Key contact quotes:
- CTO (M. Weiss): 'We can tolerate a small jitter on p50, but p99 spikes cost us conversions — need deterministic tail behavior.'
- Head of Platform (S. Rao): 'Want a single config that maps to both hosted and private installs; measurement must match what our front-end observes.'

Performance targets discussed:
- Primary SLOs: p50 <= 40ms (token-level cheap ops), p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 450ms for non-streaming 0-64 token/control requests.
- Streaming use-case: initial token latency budget (time-to-first-token) p95 <= 120ms; time-to-last-token acceptable variant depending on generation length.
- Throughput: baseline 200 req/s sustained, peak 1,200 req/s burst for 30s windows during market opens.

Measurement alignment requirements (explicit asks):
- Client-side vs server-side timing: Lindenbridge insists on client-side observed timings for SLAs (browser -> edge -> inference -> first-byte) but wants server-side hooks for debugging. Need standardized request IDs and distributed tracing.
- Streaming measurement: agree on two separate SLO streams — TTF (time-to-first-token) and completion tail for non-interactive generations. P99 measurement semantics must ignore cancelled sessions and network-induced re-transmits.
- Percentile computation: prefer sliding-window 1h windows for alerting with 24h rollups for invoicing. Need clarification on aggregation (global vs per-region vs per-route).

Proof-of-concept / POC milestones:
- 2026-02-18: Intro call (ff_2026-02-18_3456) — validated high-level fit and compliance needs.
- 2026-02-25: Technical deep-dive (ff_2026-02-25_4981) — walked through Redwood batching, KV cache, and fallback model variants.
- 2026-03-02: Synthetic load run scheduled against a dedicated 4-GPU pool (shared test infra) to validate p95 and p99 under 300 req/s baseline.
- Action item: Redwood to provide detailed measurement plan + sample dashboards; Lindenbridge to supply representative production trace samples.

Reserved GPU planning notes:
- Initial ask: sizing for a reserved pool that meets baseline throughput with 20% headroom. Early estimate: 8 x high-memory GPUs for quantized medium-sized models (internal calc attached in drive doc).
- Burst handling: discuss autoscale vs warm standby GPU nodes. Lindenbridge prefers reserved plus burst credits to avoid cold start variability.

SLA negotiation points raised by Lindenbridge legal/procurement:
- Clear definition of measured latency (client-observed vs server-observed) — legal requires client-observed for credits.
- Maintenance windows: max 4h/quarter for non-critical updates; mission-critical windows require failover to secondary region.
- Credits: tiered credits for missed p95/p99 thresholds with caps; Lindenbridge requested a performance bank model.

Open technical questions / risks:
- How will streaming p99 be computed when applications interleave multiple simultaneous streams from one client? Need examples.
- Network egress constraints for on-prem deployment — may affect client-observed timing and skew measurements.
- Model variant fallback semantics under constrained capacity (will fallback change tail behavior unpredictably?).

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to provide SLO appendix (detailed metric definitions + aggregation rules) by 2026-03-08.
- SE to run synthetic p99 test and share traces by 2026-03-12.
- Legal + Lindenbridge to send counterproposal on credits by 2026-03-19.
